issues.description: Returning a bare nil *result from run() relocates the nil-deref one frame up instead of fixing it
issues.detail: When CompareAndSwap fails and t.result.Load() returns nil, run() returns nil. Callers treat *result as non-nil, so the nil-deref is pushed upstream rather than resolved. The leader's panic-cleanup path needs a sentinel failed result with a pre-closed done channel and a Fatal error, not a nil escape hatch.

issues.description: The race between Load and use of t.result is patched inconsistently, not actually fixed
issues.detail: The pending-output branch at the top of run() still loads t.result and hands it onward without the same guard as the CAS-failed branch. The lifecycle of t.result across leader panic, CAS failure, and waiter contention is never stated. Two call sites handle the same race differently; document the invariant or use a single atomic snapshot path.

issues.description: Comment 'Leader panicked but we did see a result' contradicts the code it annotates
issues.detail: The branch fires precisely when output is nil, i.e. we did NOT see a result. Either the comment is a typo for 'did not see' or the logic is wrong. Comments that lie to the next maintainer are worse than no comments. Fix the words or fix the code.

issues.description: No regression test reproduces the leader-panic-while-waiting race
issues.detail: A concurrency fix without a deterministic reproducer is folklore. Inject a panic in the leader, have N waiters, assert they all receive a sensible error rather than nil or panic. Without this, the fix rests on inspection of code whose invariants are unstated and will regress.

issues.description: t.result overloads nil to mean too many states; encode 'leader failed' as data
issues.detail: t.result's nil currently means not-started, in-progress-leader-died, and now caller-should-bail. Overloading nil is why this race surfaced. A sentinel failed-result with a pre-closed done channel and a Fatal error would let waitUntilDone work uniformly and delete the new nil-check branch entirely.

issues.description: PR conflates a pure refactor (checkCycle extraction) with a race fix
issues.detail: The checkCycle extraction is a clean composition win, but bundling it with the race fix makes the actual behavior change harder to bisect and review. Split into two patches: one pure refactor with zero behavior change, one minimal race fix with its test. The author already plans follow-up work, so they know how to split.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. All three reviewers converge on the same core verdict: the race fix relocates the nil-deref one frame up by returning a bare nil *result from run(), while the pending-output branch handles the same race inconsistently. The comment 'Leader panicked but we did see a result' contradicts the code beneath it. The checkCycle extraction is a fine composition win and should ideally land as its own patch. No test reproduces the leader-panic-while-waiting race, leaving the fix unverified. The right shape is a sentinel failed-result with a pre-closed done channel, not nil-as-tombstone.
